level0.title: Copy code out of a chat tab
level0.line: Everyone starts here. It doesn't count, and nobody's judging.

tiers.name: First contact
tiers.line: It edits, it runs things, it answers. You stop copy-pasting.

tiers.name: Context
tiers.line: It knows what you know, because you told it.

tiers.name: Checks
tiers.line: It proves the thing works before it says done.

tiers.name: Tools
tiers.line: It reaches past the repo: CLIs, servers, your browser, your inbox.

tiers.name: Your setup
tiers.line: Rules, skills, hooks and memory that you wrote yourself.

tiers.name: Second opinions
tiers.line: Another agent reads it before you do.

tiers.name: Off the desk
tiers.line: It works while you sleep, sit on the couch, or close the laptop.

tiers.name: Orchestra
tiers.line: Many agents, one plan, and you still know who's doing what.

tiers.name: Beyond the screen
tiers.line: Your agents reach the team, the release, the pager, and the physical world.

tiers.name: Full circle
tiers.line: Fewer, sharper tools, and you understand them all the way down.

levels.title: Install a coding agent
levels.line: An agent reads your files and runs commands. A chat tab only sees what you paste into it.
levels.check: Any agent config folder exists: ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.cursor, ~/.config/opencode, ~/.gemini, ~/.factory, ~/.pi. You're reading this from inside one, so: yes.

from.name: Mitchell Hashimoto
from.q: To find value, you must use an agent.

levels.title: Let it edit your files
levels.line: No more copy-pasting between chat and editor. It writes the change, you read the diff.
levels.check: Its file-edit tool shows up in session logs (Edit, Write, apply_patch).

levels.title: Ask it how the code works
levels.line: "How does auth work here?" The fastest way into any codebase, including yours from last year.
levels.check: 5+ prompts that are questions about the code (how, why, where, what does).

from.name: Anthropic, Claude Code best practices
from.q: Ask it the questions you'd ask a senior engineer about the codebase.

levels.title: Paste the whole error
levels.line: The full stack trace or log, not your summary of it. It fixes what actually broke.
levels.check: 5+ prompts with pasted blocks or raw logs ([Pasted text …], stack traces).

levels.title: Send it a screenshot
levels.line: A picture of the broken layout beats a paragraph. "Fix this" plus an image is a whole prompt.
levels.check: 3+ prompts with an image attached ([Image #…]).

from.name: Peter Steinberger
from.q: Attaches a screenshot to a large share of his prompts; "fix padding" plus an image is enough.

levels.title: Interrupt it early
levels.line: Press Esc the moment it heads the wrong way. Redirecting beats waiting for the wrong answer.
levels.check: 5+ interrupted turns in session logs ("[Request interrupted by user]").

from.name: Peter Steinberger
from.q: Don't be afraid of stopping models mid-way.

levels.title: Point at the files
levels.line: @-mention the file or paste the path. It stops guessing where things live.
levels.check: 10+ prompts with @file mentions or explicit file paths.

levels.title: Commit small and often
levels.line: A clean git tree is your undo button. Commit before you let it loose.
levels.check: It ran git commit 5+ times in your sessions, or you use checkpoints.

levels.title: Start fresh when it's stuck
levels.line: /clear and ask again. A polluted context doesn't recover by arguing with it.
levels.check: /clear, /new or a fresh session after a failed attempt, 3+ times.

from.name: Anthropic, Claude Code best practices
from.q: After two failed corrections, /clear and write a better first prompt.

levels.title: Use it for chores, not just code
levels.line: Rename 400 photos, sort the receipts, untangle a spreadsheet. It's a computer that does what you ask.
levels.check: 1+ session in a folder that isn't a git repo (Downloads, Documents, home).

levels.title: Write a rules file
levels.line: AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md: how to build, test and run this repo. It stops asking, and stops guessing.
levels.check: An AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md or .cursor/rules in any repo you work in.

from.name: Lee Robinson
from.q: I started with zero custom rules. I only added a rules file later after the model got a few things wrong

levels.title: Write down how you like to work
levels.line: One global file for every project: your taste, your tools, your pet peeves. Applied everywhere.
levels.check: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or ~/.codex/AGENTS.md exists and isn't empty.

levels.title: Talk instead of type
levels.line: Dictate your prompts. You'll give it three times the context you'd ever bother typing.
levels.check: A dictation app is installed (Wispr Flow, superwhisper, MacWhisper, VoiceInk, OpenWhispr, Aqua, Spokenly, Handy), or prompts read like speech (um, uh, long run-ons).

from.name: Dax Raad
from.q: the thing that killed my editor for me was fast local voice models more than OpenCode

levels.title: Hand it the docs
levels.line: Paste the link to the API reference, the issue, the RFC. It reads instead of guessing from memory.
levels.check: 10+ prompts with URLs, or web fetches in session logs.

levels.title: Point at an example
levels.line: "Do it like UserCard.tsx." One good example beats a paragraph of conventions.
levels.check: Prompts that name an existing file or project to copy ("like X", "same as Y", "follow Z").

levels.title: Say what done looks like
levels.line: What's wrong, where, and how you'll know it's fixed. Then it knows when to stop.
levels.check: Prompts that state a finish line ("done when", "until", "should show").

from.name: OpenAI, Codex best practices
from.q: Goal, Context, Constraints, Done when: their prompt template.

levels.title: Ask for a plan first
levels.line: Plan mode, or "don't write code yet". Fixing a plan is ten times cheaper than fixing the diff.
levels.check: Plan mode used, or 5+ prompts asking for a plan before code.

from.name: Lee Robinson
from.q: Plan mode in Cursor is one of the most underrated features.

vs.name: Peter Steinberger
vs.q: Skips plan mode; asks for options and talks it through instead.

levels.title: Ask for three versions
levels.line: Of the UI, the name, the approach. Variants cost almost nothing now, so pick the best one.
levels.check: 5+ prompts asking for variants, options or versions.

levels.title: Let it interview you
levels.line: "Ask me questions until you understand." It builds what you meant, not what you said.
levels.check: Its ask-the-user tool used, a grill-me style skill installed, or prompts like "ask me" / "interview me".

from.name: Matt Pocock
from.q: grill-me

levels.title: Add a rule after every mistake
levels.line: When it does something dumb, put the fix in the rules file. It won't make that mistake twice.
levels.check: A rules file changed 3+ times, agent memory notes saved, or prompts like "add this to AGENTS.md".

from.name: Boris Cherny
from.q: Anytime we see Claude do something incorrectly we add it to the CLAUDE.md

levels.title: Give it a way to check its work
levels.line: Tests, a build, a screenshot to compare against. It catches its own mistakes before you do.
levels.check: 10+ prompts that ask it to verify, test, or make sure it works.

from.name: Boris Cherny
from.q: give Claude a way to verify its work… 2-3x the quality

levels.title: Write the failing test first
levels.line: Reproduce the bug in a test, watch it fail, then fix it. Proof that the fix is real.
levels.check: Prompts about failing tests, TDD or red/green, or a TDD skill installed.

from.name: Steph Ango
from.q: Verify the same fixture fails before the fix and passes afterward; do not change expectations to match buggy behavior.

levels.title: Let it use a browser
levels.line: Playwright, agent-browser or Chrome. It clicks through what it built instead of assuming it works.
levels.check: A browser MCP or skill installed, or 10+ browser-automation calls.

levels.title: Ask for proof, not "done!"
levels.line: The command it ran and the real output. A screenshot. A recording of it working.
levels.check: 5+ prompts asking for proof, screenshots or recordings of the result.

from.name: Thorsten Ball
from.q: give me irrefutable proof that this works. Dazzle me. Give me a video as proof, or something.

levels.title: Rewind instead of re-explaining
levels.line: /rewind or a checkpoint takes you back to before it went wrong. Try risky things freely.
levels.check: /rewind or a checkpoint restore used by you at least once (typed, not just mentioned).

levels.title: Let it use your CLIs
levels.line: gh, aws, stripe, supabase. "Run foo --help" and it learns the rest on its own.
levels.check: It ran 3+ different third-party CLIs (gh, aws, gcloud, vercel, netlify, stripe, supabase, wrangler, fly…).

levels.title: Pre-approve the safe commands
levels.line: An allowlist for tests, lint and git status. Fewer prompts, so you stop clicking yes to everything.
levels.check: Permission allow rules, Codex rules, or auto mode configured.

levels.title: Ask side questions without derailing
levels.line: /btw, or a second session. The answer doesn't pollute the main task.
levels.check: /btw used, or a parallel throwaway session for a quick question.

levels.title: Queue your next message
levels.line: Type the follow-up while it works. Nobody waits on anybody.
levels.check: Queued prompts in your agent's stats or logs, 20+.

levels.title: Get pinged when it's done
levels.line: A hook, a sound, a push to your phone. Then go do something else.
levels.check: A hook or script that notifies you when it's done (sound, push, notification), or a rule telling it to.

from.name: Chris McCord
from.q: when it's done work it runs a `notify msg` bash function I have

vs.name: Mitchell Hashimoto
vs.q: Turns agent notifications off, so he decides when to switch context.

levels.title: Install a skill
levels.line: Someone else's packaged know-how, loaded only when the task needs it.
levels.check: 1+ skill folder in ~/.claude/skills, ~/.codex/skills, ~/.agents/skills or a repo's .claude/skills.

levels.title: Connect a tool server (MCP)
levels.line: For the things without a good CLI: Figma, Linear, your database.
levels.check: 1+ MCP server configured.

vs.name: Peter Steinberger
vs.q: Prefers CLIs: the GitHub MCP alone ate 23k tokens of context.

levels.title: Let it open the pull request
levels.line: Branch, commit, push, description. You review instead of typing.
levels.check: It ran gh pr create (or similar) 3+ times.

levels.title: Let it deploy
levels.line: Vercel, Netlify, Fly, TestFlight. You decide who presses the last button.
levels.check: It ran a deploy CLI 3+ times.

levels.title: Save a prompt as a command
levels.line: The prompt you type every week, saved as /ship or /review.
levels.check: 1+ custom command in .claude/commands, or a user-invoked skill you wrote.

levels.title: Pick the model and effort per task
levels.line: Low effort for chores, high for the gnarly bug. Fast and cheap where it doesn't matter.
levels.check: /effort or /model switched 3+ times, or reasoning effort set in config.

levels.title: Know what you spend
levels.line: ccusage, CodexBar, /usage. Tokens are a budget; spend them on purpose.
levels.check: A usage tracker installed, or /usage, /stats, /cost used 3+ times.

levels.title: Watch the context fill up
levels.line: A status line with context, model and cost. No surprise compactions halfway through a task.
levels.check: A statusLine configured, or /context used 3+ times.

levels.title: Run two agents at once
levels.line: One on the bug, one on the feature. Twice the work while you review.
levels.check: Two sessions active in the same 10 minutes, on 5+ occasions (from prompt timestamps).

levels.title: Connect it to your messages
levels.line: Gmail, Slack, Teams, calendar. "What did I promise people this week?"
levels.check: A mail, chat or calendar connector or MCP configured (names only).

levels.title: Write your own skill
levels.line: The thing you keep explaining, written once as a SKILL.md. Every session starts knowing it.
levels.check: A skill you wrote yourself: no upstream source or lockfile entry, or it lives in your own repo.

levels.title: Use subagents
levels.line: Helpers search and read in parallel, so your main session stays focused and fast.
levels.check: 10+ subagent runs in session logs.

from.name: Alexander Embiricos
from.q: Then, when I need anything new, I say "using a subagent in parallel, do X"

levels.title: Add a hook that tidies every edit
levels.line: A formatter or linter after each write. Guaranteed, unlike "please run prettier" in a rules file.
levels.check: A post-edit hook that runs a formatter or linter.

from.name: Boris Cherny
from.q: We use a PostToolUse hook to format Claude's code.

levels.title: Add a hook that says no
levels.line: Block rm -rf, force pushes, pip when you use uv. Rules are advice; hooks are enforced.
levels.check: A pre-tool hook that blocks or guards commands.

from.name: Armin Ronacher
from.q: Replaces the bash tool with a `uv`-aware version that injects Python command shims and blocks common non-`uv` workflows.

levels.title: Let it keep notes
levels.line: Memory, notes.md, PROGRESS.md. It doesn't relearn your project every morning.
levels.check: 5+ memory notes, Codex memories on, or notes/progress files in your repos.

from.name: Simon Willison
from.q: Create a notes.md file in that folder and append notes to it as you work, tracking what you tried and anything you learned along the way.

levels.title: One rules file for every agent
levels.line: Symlink CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md. The same rules, whichever agent you open.
levels.check: A CLAUDE.md that is a symlink to, or imports, an AGENTS.md (or the other way round).

from.name: Peter Steinberger
from.q:
~/.codex/AGENTS.md -> ~/Projects/agent-scripts/AGENTS.MD
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md -> ~/Projects/agent-scripts/AGENTS.MD

levels.title: Keep the rules file small
levels.line: A map to your docs, not an encyclopedia. Every line costs context in every session.
levels.check: The rules file of the repo you work in most is under 150 lines and points to other docs for the rest.

from.name: Kent C. Dodds
from.q: This file is included in full context for every agent conversation. Keep it tiny and stable.

levels.title: Write the spec first
levels.line: Two paragraphs in, a SPEC.md out, and a fresh session builds from the spec.
levels.check: A SPEC.md, PLAN.md or plans/ folder in a repo you work in.

from.name: Alex Kladov
from.q: I was providing structure, Claude was painting by the numbers.

levels.title: Have it write a handoff
levels.line: Before the context fills, it writes down where it is. The next session picks up in one read.
levels.check: A PROGRESS.md, HANDOFF.md or todo.md, or a handoff skill.

from.name: Thomas Ptacek
from.q: I should be able to tell a future agent "read PLAN.md and PROGRESS.md" and trust it's up to speed with this codebase.

levels.title: One worktree per agent
levels.line: Parallel agents in one checkout trip over each other. Worktrees keep them apart.
levels.check: git worktree list shows 2+ in any repo.

from.name: Boris Cherny
from.q: Worktrees are essential… dozens of Claudes

vs.name: Peter Steinberger (2025, he uses them now)
vs.q: Why not worktrees? I run one dev server, as I evolve my project I click through it and test multiple changes at once.

levels.title: Have an agent review the diff
levels.line: /code-review, Codex /review, a fresh session. Before you read it, not instead of you.
levels.check: A review command, review skill or review subagent used 3+ times.

from.name: Filippo Valsorda
from.q: making a human review a change before an LLM is disrespectful.

levels.title: Review with a different model
levels.line: Claude writes, GPT reviews, or the other way round. Different models miss different things.
levels.check: One vendor's agent asked to review another's work (codex exec / claude -p review, or prompts that hand a diff across).

from.name: DHH
from.q: Review this with claude

levels.title: Review with fresh eyes
levels.line: A new session or a subagent: "read this as if you didn't write it." It stops defending its own code.
levels.check: Reviews run in a fresh context (a new session or a subagent), not in the session that wrote the code.

from.name: Harper Reed
from.q: carefully read over all of the new code you just wrote … with "fresh eyes," looking super carefully for any obvious bugs … Use a subagent.

levels.title: Make it quiz you on the change
levels.line: It explains the diff, then asks you five questions. Merge only when you pass.
levels.check: An explain-diff or quiz skill, or prompts asking it to explain or quiz you on a change.

from.name: Thariq Shihipar
from.q: I only merge after I pass the quiz perfectly.

levels.title: Ask for a diagram
levels.line: Architecture, data flow, the state machine. Pictures review faster than prose.
levels.check: 3+ prompts asking for a diagram, chart or visual explanation.

from.name: Dex Horthy
from.q: /show-me prompts the agent to use concise visuals to explain what's happening, instead of walls of prose.

levels.title: Let it babysit the PR
levels.line: It watches CI and the review bots, fixes, pushes, and repeats until it's green.
levels.check: It checked CI or PR status (gh pr checks, gh run) 5+ times.

levels.title: Two agents, two jobs
levels.line: Claude writes the code, Codex draws the images. Or one builds and the other reviews.
levels.check: One agent launched another (codex exec, claude -p, gemini -p) 3+ times.

levels.title: Run it headless in scripts
levels.line: claude -p, codex exec. Logs in, JSON out, part of your scripts.
levels.check: 3+ headless runs in shell history or logs.

levels.title: Have it make a video
levels.line: A 30-second motion explainer of what you shipped, for the colleague who won't read the PR.
levels.check: Remotion, Hyperframes or ffmpeg renders from a session, or a video skill installed.

levels.title: Skip the prompts, inside a box
levels.line: Full autonomy in a container or a fresh VM with no prod keys. All the speed, none of the risk.
levels.check: Permission prompts off AND a sandbox (devcontainer, Docker, VM, /sandbox). Prompts off without a box doesn't count.

from.name: David Crawshaw
from.q: You have to turn off the sandbox, which means you have to provide your own sandbox. I have tried just about everything and I highly recommend: use a fresh VM.

levels.title: Schedule a prompt
levels.line: For later, or every morning: /loop, /schedule, cron. Work starts without you.
levels.check: A scheduled or recurring agent run (loop/cron tools, a launchd or cron entry that calls an agent).

levels.title: Let it work while you sleep
levels.line: Start a few tasks before bed, review them with coffee.
levels.check: Agent activity between 1am and 6am while you typed nothing.

from.name: Calvin French-Owen
from.q: This is over-hyped on Twitter, but I do really try and kick off 3-4 tasks in Codex before going to bed, so they'll be ready for review in the morning.

levels.title: Drive it from your phone
levels.line: Remote Control, the Codex app, ssh and tmux. Unblock it from the couch.
levels.check: Remote control set up, a mobile session, or mosh/Tailscale used to reach your agent box.

from.name: Harper Reed
from.q: Claude Code is better on your phone

levels.title: Hand chores to a cloud agent
levels.line: Codex cloud, Claude on the web, Cursor background agents. The boring stuff, no laptop needed.
levels.check: Cloud or remote agent tasks in your history.

from.name: Adam Wathan
from.q: I feed this thing every little random tedious OSS task that I'd otherwise neglect on my TODO list

levels.title: Give it a finish line it can't fake
levels.line: "Don't stop until the test passes and the screenshot matches." Then let it run.
levels.check: 3+ prompts like "don't stop until" / "keep going until", or a goal set with /goal.

levels.title: Run it in a loop
levels.line: The same prompt, fresh context, again and again until the spec is done.
levels.check: A shell loop or script that re-runs an agent, or /loop until a condition.

from.name: Geoffrey Huntley
from.q: while :; do cat PROMPT.md | claude-code ; done

levels.title: Put an agent in CI
levels.line: @claude on issues, a review on every PR. A teammate with a GitHub login.
levels.check: claude-code-action, codex action or similar in a .github/workflows file.

levels.title: Run it four times, keep the best
levels.line: The same task in parallel, thirty seconds each to judge. Throwing work away is cheap now.
levels.check: The same task run in 2+ parallel sessions or worktrees.

from.name: Alexander Embiricos
from.q: So I might kind of throw throw codex at it but I might just do it four times in parallel instead.

levels.title: Make two agents argue
levels.line: One proposes, one attacks, until they agree or you see exactly why they can't. Nice.
levels.check: Multi-round back-and-forth between two agents (rounds of review and fix, or relayed replies).

from.name: Dex Horthy
from.q: let sol and fable implement / review / argue over night

levels.title: Keep a machine that never sleeps
levels.line: A Mac mini, a VPS, a shed. Agents keep running when your laptop closes.
levels.check: Agents running on another machine you reach over ssh.

from.name: DHH
from.q: all my agent and compile work now happens on an AI shed.

levels.title: Run five at once
levels.line: Five agents on five problems, and you still know what each one is doing.
levels.check: 5+ sessions or background agents running at the same time.

levels.title: Let one agent coordinate the rest
levels.line: It hands out the work, checks on the others, and reports back to you.
levels.check: One agent messaging or steering others (agent teams, SendMessage, an orchestrator session).

from.name: Andreas Kling
from.q: Tell coordinator to parallelize the work over 4 separate computers via SSH

levels.title: Strong model plans, fast model builds
levels.line: Pay for thinking where it matters, and for speed everywhere else.
levels.check: Per-agent model settings, or 3+ prompts assigning models to roles.

from.name: Steve Yegge
from.q: Every implementation bead goes through this lifecycle: Fable design, Opus implementation, Fable review.

levels.title: Give agents job titles
levels.line: A security reviewer, a tester, a docs writer, each with its own tools and model.
levels.check: 2+ custom agent definitions (.claude/agents/*.md or equivalent).

levels.title: Script the whole pipeline
levels.line: A rerunnable multi-agent workflow instead of one heroic session.
levels.check: A workflow tool used, or a script that chains several agent runs.

levels.title: Hire adversarial reviewers
levels.line: Two refuters per builder, and points for every real bug. They try hard.
levels.check: Reviews run by 2+ competing or adversarial agents.

from.name: Jesse Vincent
from.q: Assign two subagents to review your work adversarially. Tell them that whoever finds the largest number of legitimate significant issues gets 5 points.

levels.title: Three bug hunters, one report
levels.line: Several reviewers in parallel, then one agent rules out the false positives.
levels.check: Findings from 2+ review tools merged into one triaged list.

from.name: Nolan Lawson
from.q: Run a Claude sub-agent, Codex, and Cursor Bugbot to find bugs in this PR ranked by critical/high/medium/low.

levels.title: Make every task teach the next
levels.line: After each job it writes the lesson into a skill or rule, so the next one is cheaper.
levels.check: Rules, skills or memory edited by agent sessions 5+ times.

from.name: Kieran Klaassen
from.q: Compound is still the most important step, because the whole point is that every feature should make the next feature easier.

levels.title: Turn rules into checks
levels.line: Wrote "never do X" twice? Make it a lint rule or a type, so it can't happen.
levels.check: Custom lint rules, ast-grep rules or check scripts in a repo.

from.name: José Valim
from.q: encode as many rules as possible into deterministic checks (first) and adversarial reviews (second), instead of relying exclusively on a bunch of AGENTS.md files to do the job.

levels.title: Build a tool for your agent
levels.line: A small CLI made for it to call: --json output, good --help, no prompts.
levels.check: Your own scripts or CLIs that agents call regularly.

levels.title: Test your skills
levels.line: Does it trigger when it should, and does it actually help? An eval tells you.
levels.check: Eval files for a skill or plugin, or a plugin eval run.

levels.title: Publish your skills
levels.line: A public repo of your skills, so your team, or strangers, can use them.
levels.check: Your skills live in a git repo with a remote.

from.name: Peter Steinberger
from.q: agent-scripts

levels.title: Put an agent in the team chat
levels.line: Tag it in Slack and it opens the PR. Teammates use it without installing anything.
levels.check: A chat-integrated agent set up (Slack app, Claude Tag, Devin, a bot).

from.name: Cat Wu and Thariq Shihipar, via Simon Willison
from.q: Claude Tag lands 65% of the Claude Code team's product PRs.

levels.title: Make something physical
levels.line: It designs the 3D-printable part, the enclosure, the bracket. Code that ends up on your desk.
levels.check: OpenSCAD, CadQuery, build123d or Blender driven by the agent, or .stl, .3mf or .scad files it produced.

levels.title: Give your agents a wiki about you
levels.line: How you think, what you've decided, what you can't stand. Loaded only when it's relevant.
levels.check: A personal context repo or folder that your agents load when relevant, through a rule or a skill.

levels.title: Let your agents talk to each other
levels.line: No more "Codex says: [paste]". They pass findings directly while you do something else.
levels.check: Agents sending each other messages or reading each other's output, without you relaying it.

levels.title: Let it use your computer
levels.line: It clicks through desktop apps, the simulator, your logged-in browser. Not just files and a terminal.
levels.check: Computer-use or desktop-control tools used: computer use, Peekaboo, Claude in Chrome, simulator control.

levels.title: Give it a release checklist
levels.line: Every release, the same long QA script, run start to finish by the agent.
levels.check: A QA or release checklist file, or a release skill.

from.name: Salvatore Sanfilippo
from.q: QA_BEFORE_RELEASES.md

levels.title: Put it on call
levels.line: It watches errors and alerts, and has a fix open before you've read the page.
levels.check: An error-tracking or alerting connector (Sentry, Datadog, PagerDuty, Grafana) or alerts sent into an agent session.

levels.title: Build on an agent SDK
levels.line: Your own agent product, with the same loop the big ones use under the hood.
levels.check: An agent SDK in a project's dependencies (Claude Agent SDK, Codex SDK, OpenAI Agents).

levels.title: Delete more config than you add
levels.line: Prune the rules, skills and servers that don't earn their tokens anymore.
levels.check: A rules file that got shorter at least once in its git history.

from.name: Dax Raad
from.q: when i see people with custom workflows and setups they're all addressing problems that don't exist anymore

levels.title: Review by risk, not by habit
levels.line: A copy fix gets a glance. Auth, money and migrations get every line.
levels.check: Your rules or review setup name the paths that always get a human read.

from.name: Boris Cherny
from.q: I read diffs when it's touching critical code, or code that's important to get right. I don't write the code.

vs.name: Mitchell Hashimoto
vs.q: First, I reviewed the entire diff (yes, all ~3,000 lines of it). Then I reviewed it again. I re-read the entire diff by hand three or four times.

levels.title: Teach it when to stop and ask
levels.line: A stuck agent asks instead of trying a ninth fix. You set that up.
levels.check: A rule or hook that makes it stop and report when stuck or out of scope.

levels.title: Make your git log obey your rules
levels.line: If the rules say "no AI trailers" or "tests pass", the last 100 commits agree.
levels.check: Compare what your global rules demand with your last 100 commits (trailers, messages). They agree.

from.name: Mike McQuaid
from.q: reject "has AI attribution; remove it and disclose AI use in the PR description."

levels.title: Give it its own identity
levels.line: Its own GitHub account and scoped keys, so you can always see, and revoke, what it did.
levels.check: Commits or PRs in your repos by a bot account you run, or a separate login the agent uses.

from.name: Anthony Fu
from.q: Agents on behave of @antfu

levels.title: Put hardware in the loop
levels.line: It flashes the board, reads the serial port, watches the LED, and checks its own work.
levels.check: Device tools driven by an agent (serial, adb, simctl, esptool, arduino-cli…).

from.name: Linus Torvalds
from.q: I started the day with "I want to connect two pedals together and have them validate each other", and ended the day with three pedals, a signal generator, and a USB MIDI dongle all connected together as a validation bench with automated checks.

levels.title: Run it on a local model
levels.line: Open weights on your own machine: private, offline, and nobody can take it away.
levels.check: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or MLX installed, and an agent pointed at a local model.

levels.title: Run your own harness
levels.line: Pi, OpenClaw, Hermes, or one you built. You choose the tools, the prompts and the loop.
levels.check: Pi, OpenClaw, Hermes or a harness you wrote, installed and in use.

from.name: Peter Steinberger
from.q: I use OpenClaw (which uses Codex) and web sessions.

levels.title: Let it improve your setup
levels.line: A scheduled agent reads your recent sessions, finds the friction, and fixes your rules and skills.
levels.check: A recurring agent run that reviews past sessions and edits rules or skills, or /insights used to change your setup.

from.name: OpenAI, Codex best practices
from.q: Schedule a review of recent chats to find friction, then fix prompts and setup.

levels.title: Write your own agent
levels.line: A model, a loop and a few tools, in a few hundred lines. After that, nothing on this list is magic.
levels.check: A project of yours that calls a model API with tools in a loop you wrote, not only an SDK or someone else's harness.

from.name: Thorsten Ball
from.q: It’s an LLM, a loop, and enough tokens.

pi.title: Say please
pi.line: Doesn't help. Doesn't hurt. Doesn't count. You get a π on your card anyway.

fossils.title: "You are a senior engineer with 20 years of experience."
fossils.line: Role-play preambles. Today's models don't need the pep talk; they need the context.

fossils.title: "I'll tip you $200 for a perfect answer."
fossils.line: It sort of worked once. Nobody ever paid.

fossils.title: "Take a deep breath and work on this step by step."
fossils.line: Reasoning models think before answering anyway.

fossils.title: "Write the full code. No placeholders."
fossils.line: From the era of lazy models and "// rest of the code stays the same".

fossils.title: .cursorrules
fossils.line: One file in the repo root. Replaced by rule folders and AGENTS.md, which every agent reads.

fossils.title: "ultrathink"
fossils.line: Thinking keywords. Effort is a setting now, and reports disagree on whether the word still does anything.

fossils.title: "How many r's are in strawberry?"
fossils.line: Retired as a benchmark. Still a good party trick.
